stages.title: AI compute hall
stages.summary: The room inside the data center where racks of AI servers sit. Facility power and outdoor cooling enter at the edges; this page focuses on the gear inside the hall — chips, boxes, fabrics, and liquid cooling — not the grid transformers and chillers covered under Electrification.

companies.name: Equinix / Digital Realty (colo landlords)
companies.note: Own many halls that host hyperscaler and neocloud racks — see Hyperscalers

companies.name: Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Meta, …)
companies.note: Design and operate dedicated AI halls — see Hyperscalers section

stages.title: Server rack
stages.summary: A tall frame that holds servers, networking, power shelves, and often liquid-cooling manifolds. AI racks can draw tens of kilowatts; liquid cooling and dense power shelves are common. Rack-scale GPU systems (for example NVIDIA NVL-class designs) treat the whole rack as one compute unit.

companies.note: AI racks and liquid-cooled rack designs

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.note: PowerEdge racks and enterprise AI systems

companies.name: Foxconn / Quanta / Wiwynn
companies.note: ODM rack and tray assembly for cloud buyers

stages.title: Server / blade chassis
stages.summary: The metal box (1U–4U or a tray in a rack-scale system) that holds the motherboard, accelerators, memory, network cards, local storage, and power supplies. OEMs brand and support them; ODMs often design and assemble the boards.

companies.name: Super Micro Computer
companies.note: Custom AI servers; often first with new GPU platforms

stages.title: Motherboard / PCB materials
stages.summary: High-speed server and switch boards need low-loss copper-clad laminates (CCL), specialty glass cloth, and ultra-smooth copper foil. These materials sit under every AI motherboard and switch PCB — supply-tight inputs as lane rates climb.

companies.note: Leading low-loss copper-clad laminate (CCL) for AI server and switch boards

companies.name: Mitsui Kinzoku
companies.note: HVLP / carrier copper foil for high-speed laminates (supply-tight input)

companies.name: Nitto Boseki (Nittobo)
companies.note: Low-CTE T-glass / low-Dk glass cloth; reported shortage gating substrates and high-speed PCBs

companies.name: Taiwan Union Technology (TUC)

companies.name: WUS Printed Circuit

stages.title: GPUs (graphics processing units)
stages.summary: Merchant accelerators that do most of the matrix math for training and inference. They sit on the board or as modules (SXM / OAM-class) next to HBM stacks. Software stacks such as CUDA make ecosystem lock-in as important as raw silicon.

companies.name: Qualcomm
companies.note: AI200/AI250 card/rack plans in industry roadmaps

stages.title: Custom AI ASICs
stages.summary: Application-specific integrated circuits designed with or for one hyperscaler (TPUs, Trainium, Maia, MTIA, and peers). They trade generality for efficiency at that buyer’s workloads. Broadcom and Marvell often design the silicon; foundries and packaging are under Semiconductors.

companies.note: Custom AI ASICs for hyperscalers + switch silicon

companies.note: AWS custom training and inference chips

companies.note: Meta Training and Inference Accelerator programs

companies.note: Custom AI ASIC partner (Google TPU program and peers)

companies.name: Alchip Technologies
companies.note: TSMC-ecosystem ASIC design house for hyperscaler accelerators

companies.name: Global Unichip (GUC)
companies.note: TSMC-affiliated ASIC design service with CoWoS/HBM integration

stages.title: FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays)
stages.summary: Reconfigurable chips used for networking offload, smart NICs, prototyping, and some inference or preprocessing jobs where fixed ASICs are not ready yet. Less dominant than GPUs for large training, but important in the I/O path.

companies.name: Altera (Silver Lake 51% / Intel 49%)
companies.note: Standalone FPGA company after Silver Lake took 51% control (Sep 2025); Intel retains 49%. IPO filing reported Sep 2026 — still private as of this page.

stages.title: Server CPUs
stages.summary: Host processors that run the operating system, drivers, and non-accelerator work. x86 (AMD EPYC, Intel Xeon) still dominate many AI servers; Arm designs grow where power efficiency matters.

companies.name: Ampere Computing
companies.note: Arm server CPUs for cloud efficiency

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.note: Arm AGI CPU (up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores; Meta lead partner, Mar 2026) plus architecture IP licensed into server CPUs — no longer IP-licensor only

companies.name: NVIDIA (Grace / Vera)
companies.note: Grace (GB200/GB300) and Vera (Vera Rubin) Arm host CPUs in NVIDIA rack-scale AI systems

stages.title: HBM — high-bandwidth memory
stages.summary: Stacked DRAM dies sitting next to the GPU or ASIC so the accelerator is not starved for data. Through roughly 2027, HBM supply and yields are a primary throttle on how many leading accelerators can ship (see Scarcity on this page).

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.note: Leading HBM supplier to major GPU programs (US ADR SKHY)

stages.title: DRAM / system RAM
stages.summary: Ordinary server memory on DIMMs that holds the CPU’s working set, OS, and framework state. Separate from HBM on the accelerator package, but still a large BOM line as node counts grow.

stages.title: NICs & SmartNICs
stages.summary: Network interface cards that attach the server to Ethernet or InfiniBand. SmartNICs / DPUs offload encryption, virtualization, and some collective communication so CPUs and GPUs stay on useful work.

stages.title: Local / near-node storage
stages.summary: SSDs inside the server or JBOF shelves next to the rack for checkpoints, datasets, and scratch space. Bulk nearline hard drives and flash arrays deeper in the hall are listed under Memory & storage on this page.

companies.name: Sandisk
companies.note: NAND / SSD flash spun from Western Digital (Feb 2025); WDC remains HDD-focused

companies.note: Top-3 NAND maker (Sandisk JV); TSE Prime since Dec 2024

companies.note: NAND / SSD flash alongside DRAM and HBM

stages.title: Server / shelf power supplies (PSUs)
stages.summary: In-rack AC–DC CRPS shelves and emerging DC–DC / 800 VDC in-row shelves that feed motherboard and accelerator rails before board VRMs take over. Today most AI racks still ship high-wattage redundant AC PSUs; as sidecar ±400/800 VDC (~H2 2026–2027) and native 800 V racks ramp (~2028–29+), classic AC shelves are designed around. Facility SST, MV transformers, and hall DC busway live under Electrification — do not double-count here. Educational orientation only — not investment advice.

stages.title: VRMs & board / tray power stages
stages.summary: Voltage regulator modules, intermediate DC–DC modules, and power-management ICs that take shelf or 48/54 V rails down to GPU/CPU core voltages at high current. Distinct from facility UPS, switchgear, and SST systems (Electrification) and from SiC/GaN device fab (Semiconductor Fabrication). Amp-density and thermal headroom already matter on leading AI boards; 48 V and 800→intermediate module volume thickens with sidecar ~2027+. Educational orientation only — not investment advice.

companies.name: Vicor
companies.note: High-density 800 V / ±400 V → 48/54 V modular DC–DC inside AI racks
companies.demand_when: As 800 VDC / ±400 V sidecar and native racks scale from ~2027
companies.demand_for: High-density modular DC–DC conversion from 800 V / ±400 V down to intermediate buses inside AI racks and trays
companies.why_critical: Facility-level 800 V only helps if rack modules efficiently step to intermediate buses without reclaiming the copper/thermal budget
companies.why_there: Smaller pure-play module vendor vs megacap systems OEMs; 800 V rack-module demand narrative still early relative to loud systems names
companies.demand_detail: When: As 800 VDC / ±400 V sidecar and native racks scale from ~2027. For what: High-density modular DC–DC from 800 V / ±400 V → 48/54 V inside AI racks. Why critical: Facility 800 V only helps if rack modules step efficiently to intermediate buses. Why here: Smaller pure-play vs megacap systems OEMs; narrative still early. Orientation only — not advice.

stages.title: Top-of-rack (ToR) switch
stages.summary: The first network hop for servers in a rack — usually Ethernet today, sometimes InfiniBand. Concentrates many server links into fewer uplinks toward leaf/spine or GPU fabrics.

companies.name: NVIDIA (Spectrum / InfiniBand)
companies.note: Ethernet and InfiniBand ToR / leaf options

stages.title: In-rack cables (DAC / copper)
stages.summary: Short copper cables (direct-attach copper, backplanes, and high-speed harnesses) that link servers to the ToR switch and link GPUs inside a rack-scale domain (NVLink copper domains, for example). Lowest latency for very short reaches.

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.note: Active electrical cables (AECs) and retimers for in-rack / scale-up copper

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.note: PCIe / CXL / Ethernet retimers for AI lane rates

stages.title: In-rack / short-reach optics
stages.summary: Pluggable or onboard optical modules for short hops inside a rack or between adjacent chassis when copper cannot meet density or reach. Overlaps Photonics; products are often 100G–1.6T-class transceivers and emerging co-packaged optics.

companies.name: Lumentum
companies.note: Lasers / optical engines — see Photonics scarcity

companies.name: InnoLight (Zhongji Innolight)
companies.note: Largest 800G/1.6T transceiver supplier; NVIDIA CPO partner. On the US DoD 1260H list as of 8 Jun 2026 (procurement limits from 30 Jun 2026; goods containing its products from 30 Jun 2027).

companies.name: Eoptolink
companies.note: Top-3 AI transceiver supplier; named NVIDIA CPO partner

companies.name: Fabrinet
companies.note: Precision optical module assembly / manufacturing partner

companies.name: Sumitomo Electric
companies.note: InP substrates, lasers, fiber and connectors; named NVIDIA CPO partner

stages.title: Between-rack fabric (leaf / spine / GPU fabric)
stages.summary: The network that stitches many racks into one training or inference cluster — Ethernet leaf/spine, InfiniBand, or proprietary GPU fabrics (NVLink domains extended with switches). Product lines differ from pure ToR boxes even when the brand is the same.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.note: Merchant switch ASICs inside many fabrics

stages.title: Between-rack / row optical interconnect
stages.summary: Longer optical links (fiber + transceivers + optical DSPs) that span rows or halls when copper runs out of reach or power budget. Expected to become a dominant pinch around 2027–2028 after packaging and HBM ease — deep map under Photonics.

companies.name: AXT
companies.note: InP / compound substrates upstream of lasers

stages.title: Direct-to-chip cold plates
stages.summary: Metal plates with coolant channels mounted on GPUs and CPUs. Heat moves into liquid instead of air heatsinks. First hardware touchpoint of liquid cooling on the silicon.

companies.name: CoolIT (Ecolab)
companies.note: Direct liquid cooling cold plates and loops — Ecolab closed ~$4.75B CoolIT acquisition Jul 2026

companies.name: Eaton (Boyd Thermal)
companies.note: Cold plates, CDUs and liquid loops after Eaton’s $9.5B Boyd Thermal deal (closed Mar 2026)

companies.name: LG Electronics
companies.note: NVIDIA DSX Ready CDU / liquid-cooling path (also CDU stage)

stages.title: Blade / tray coolant loop
stages.summary: Hoses, quick-disconnects, and manifolds that collect cold-plate loops inside one server or GPU tray and present a single pair of fittings to the rack. Leak detection and serviceability matter as much as thermal performance.

companies.name: CoolIT (Ecolab)
companies.note: Tray-level manifolds, QD couplings and liquid loops (Ecolab / CoolIT)

companies.name: Eaton (Boyd Thermal)
companies.note: Tray-level liquid loops and thermal hardware (Boyd Thermal under Eaton)

companies.name: Asetek
companies.note: Direct-to-chip tray loops and QD couplings

companies.name: Server OEMs & ODMs
companies.note: Design the tray plumbing into shipped SKUs

stages.title: Rack coolant manifold
stages.summary: Vertical or rear manifolds that daisy-chain many servers’ liquid loops to shared supply/return pipes. Often paired with rear-door heat exchangers on air-assisted racks.

stages.title: CDU — coolant distribution unit
stages.summary: A skid that pumps and conditions facility or secondary loop coolant, controls temperature and flow, and isolates IT liquid loops from building chilled water. One CDU often serves a row or a set of high-density racks.

stages.title: Heat exchanger to facility cooling
stages.summary: Where IT coolant hands heat to building chilled water, dry coolers, or outside air systems. This is the boundary with facility HVAC covered under Electrification — still shown here so the liquid path is complete.

stages.title: Immersion cooling (optional path)
stages.summary: Servers submerged in dielectric fluid instead of (or besides) cold plates. Useful for very high densities or retrofit cases; still a smaller share than direct-to-chip liquid in most AI deployments today.
